questions.stem: In the equation Q = mcΔT, what does 'm' represent when measuring the enthalpy change of a reaction in solution?

options.text: The mass of the solid reactant added
The mass of the solution being heated
The molar mass of the products

questions.explanation: In Q = mcΔT, 'm' is the mass of the substance being heated, which is usually the solution (often assumed to be water). It is not the mass of the solid reactant. The density of the solution is typically assumed to be 1 g/cm³.
